hook.text: Both study people. But sociologists survey cities while anthropologists live in villages for a year.

buildup.text: Sociology focuses on modern, large-scale societies. Anthropology historically studied small-scale, non-Western ones.

discovery.text: Anthropologists use immersive fieldwork. Sociologists prefer surveys, statistics, and large data sets.

twist.text: Today the boundary blurs. Anthropologists study corporations; sociologists study tribes. Methods overlap.

climax.text: The real difference is perspective: sociology asks how society works; anthropology asks what makes us human.

quiz.question: What traditionally distinguished anthropology from sociology?
options: Anthropology used immersive fieldwork in small-scale societies

details.summary: Anthropology and sociology both study human social life but differ in scope and method. Sociology typically focuses on modern industrial societies using quantitative methods, while anthropology examines all human societies using ethnographic fieldwork and cross-cultural comparison.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding the distinction helps students choose the right discipline for their questions. Anthropology's broader scope and immersive methods offer perspectives on human diversity that sociology's more narrowly focused quantitative approach does.
takeaways: Sociology focuses on modern industrial societies using quantitative methods
Anthropology examines all societies using ethnography and comparison
Both study social life but differ in scope and methodology

faq.question: What are the main methodological differences?
faq.answer: Sociology emphasizes surveys, statistics, and quantitative analysis of large populations. Anthropology emphasizes ethnographic fieldwork, qualitative analysis, and deep contextual understanding of specific communities. Both disciplines increasingly borrow each other's methods as boundaries blur.

faq.question: Can the two disciplines be combined?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Many scholars work across both disciplines. Some universities combine them into joint departments. Anthropological ethnography enriches sociological theory, while sociological quantitative rigor strengthens anthropological generalizations.
